response.title: Do I need a 240 volt inverter for a small off-grid cabin, or is a simpler 120 volt one enough for lights, a fridge and a small air conditioner?
response.answer:
A 120V inverter is probably all you need for a small off-grid cabin running lights, a refrigerator, and a small air conditioner. You generally only need a 240V inverter if you have appliances specifically requiring 240V.

For a typical US cabin, I'd recommend a 120V pure sine wave inverter rated around 3,000W, assuming you're using an efficient, small air conditioner.

The important consideration is that refrigerators and air conditioners have compressors that can briefly draw significantly more power when starting.

A 2,000W inverter may also work if your AC is particularly efficient and its starting surge is modest.

I'd lean toward a 48V battery system for a 3,000W inverter because it reduces DC current and makes wiring more manageable. Use appropriately rated DC protection, grounding, and electrical distribution equipment.

One important distinction

Inverter wattage determines how much equipment you can run simultaneously. Battery capacity determines how long you can run it.

| Small window AC (5,000–8,000 BTU) | 450–900W |
| Phone chargers, router, etc. | 30–100W |
| **Total running load** | **610–1,260W** |

The important consideration is that refrigerators and air conditioners have compressors that can briefly draw significantly more power when starting.

## 120V vs. 240V for your cabin

| Feature | 120V inverter | 120/240V split-phase inverter |
|---|---|---|
| LED lighting | Yes | Yes |
| Standard refrigerator | Yes | Yes |
| Small window AC | Yes | Yes |
| Standard outlets | Yes | Yes |
| 240V well pump | No | Yes |
| Electric stove / dryer | Usually no | Yes |
| Cost and complexity | Generally lower | Generally higher |
